solutionSource.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

entries.clue: Riddle gripping western author (5)

indicatorNotes.gripping: the first word holds the second tight inside it

blocks.note: to riddle is to sieve, to sift
W = western, held inside SIFT after the S

annotation.surface: A puzzle has got its hands on a writer of cowboy stories.
annotation.walkthrough: A riddle is also a coarse sieve, so the word is a verb here, not a puzzle. Jonathan Swift wrote Gulliver's Travels.
annotation.definitionFit: Jonathan Swift, the Irish satirist behind Gulliver's Travels, is one of the best-known authors in English.

entries.clue: Temporarily change course with road vehicle going over underground passage (6)

annotation.definition: road vehicle going over underground passage

blocks.note: to sub is to substitute for a while
a way is a course or route

annotation.surface: Traffic is diverted while a tunnel is being dug under the road.
annotation.walkthrough: The definition describes the thing: a passage under a road, with the traffic passing overhead. 'Change course' looks like a diversion, but it is two separate pieces.
annotation.definitionFit: In Britain a subway is a pedestrian tunnel beneath a busy road, so vehicles pass over the walkers below.

entries.clue: Manufacturer in clay sounded a pragmatic sort (13)

indicatorNotes.sounded: a word that is sounded is spoken, so we want its sound, not its spelling

blocks.note: used as it stands
clay and dust both mean the mortal body, as in 'dust to dust'
a realist is a pragmatic person; said quickly it matches the end of the answer

annotation.surface: A factory owner, covered in clay, came across as a practical type.
annotation.walkthrough: Only the last part is heard rather than spelt: REALIST, run into the rest, gives the ending -RIALIST.
annotation.definitionFit: An industrialist owns or runs manufacturing businesses, so the two nouns are interchangeable.

entries.clue: Wind awfully wet around home (5)

indicatorNotes.awfully: something done awfully is done badly, so the letters are mangled
indicatorNotes.around: the mixed letters go around the next piece

blocks.note: WET rearranged, split around IN
to be in is to be at home

annotation.surface: A complaint about foul, rainy weather blowing round the house.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Wind' looks like the weather, which the surface encourages; it is the verb, rhyming with 'find'.
annotation.definitionFit: To twine is to wind or twist something around something else, as a creeper does round a post.

entries.clue: Lively piece with the oud centrally in a north African style (10)

indicatorNotes.centrally: take what sits at the centre of each word

blocks.note: the middle letter of THE
the middle letter of OUD
moresque means in the Moorish style

annotation.surface: A description of a sprightly tune played on the oud, the Arab lute, in Moroccan fashion.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Centrally' works on both short words: the centre of THE and the centre of OUD. Moresque decoration or music is Moorish, from north-west Africa.
annotation.definitionFit: A humoresque is a short, light-hearted piece of music, Dvořák's being the famous one.

entries.clue: Stolen by chief tearaway (7)

blocks.note: hot goods are stolen ones
head = chief; 'by' sets it beside HOT

annotation.surface: Loot taken by a gang leader who is a wild young thing.
annotation.walkthrough: HOT is slang for stolen, as in hot property.
annotation.definitionFit: A tearaway is a reckless, impetuous person, which is exactly what a hothead is.

entries.clue: List tall plant coming up in spring month for controlling (12)

indicatorNotes.coming up: in a down answer, rising means the letters read bottom to top
indicatorNotes.in: the reversed letters go inside the month

blocks.note: MAY, opened after its A
a rota is a list of duties
the lupin is a tall spiky garden flower
the end of MAY, closing round the reversal

annotation.surface: Instructions for which tall flowers to plant during May.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Coming up' works because this is a down answer: the list and the flower are read bottom to top, then slotted between the A and Y of the month.
annotation.definitionFit: Manipulatory behaviour controls others by influence or trickery, so it is controlling in that sense.

entries.clue: Royal Engineers find supply for facility (8)

blocks.note: the usual abbreviation for the army corps
to source something is to find a supply of it

annotation.surface: Army engineers are tasked with getting materials for a new base.
annotation.walkthrough: SOURCE is the verb here, as a buyer uses it: to find where something can be got.
annotation.definitionFit: A resource is something available to be drawn on, much as a facility is a provision or amenity.

entries.clue: Skier’s first drunk melting snow (5)

indicatorNotes.first: only the opening letter of the word is taken

blocks.note: the first letter of skier
a lush is a drunkard

annotation.surface: An après-ski tale: the first skier down is tipsy, and the snow is going soft.
annotation.walkthrough: LUSH is slang for a heavy drinker, a noun that stands in for 'drunk'.
annotation.definitionFit: Slush is snow that has partly melted into wet, grey mush.

entries.clue: What picnic might be free? (10)

blocks.note: the joke reading: a picnic that has lost its wicker basket
the plain meaning: not held back

annotation.surface: A question about a picnic that costs nothing.
annotation.walkthrough: The joke splits the word: a hamper is the wicker picnic basket, so a picnic without one is UN-HAMPERED. 'Free' looks like 'costing nothing' and means unrestricted.
annotation.definitionFit: To be unhampered is to be free of anything that holds you back.

entries.clue: Uproar remains to west of America (6)

indicatorNotes.to west of: in an across answer, west is the left, so this piece comes first

blocks.note: a rump is what remains of a larger body, like a rump parliament
the United States

annotation.surface: A news line: a noisy dispute is still going on in the west of the States.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Remains' looks like a verb (is still there); it is the noun, a remnant, which gives RUMP.
annotation.definitionFit: A rumpus is a noisy disturbance or commotion, an uproar.

entries.clue: Actor appearing in Faust in Oviedo? (7)

indicatorNotes.appearing in: the name shows up inside the words that follow

blocks.note: the actor's name runs from the U of Faust to the V of Oviedo

annotation.surface: Casting news: a star is to play Faust in a Spanish city.
annotation.walkthrough: Oviedo is a city in northern Spain. Peter Ustinov won two Oscars and played Poirot.
annotation.definitionFit: Sir Peter Ustinov was a British actor, writer and raconteur.

entries.clue: Wine book in which some have invested (9)

blocks.note: the fortified wine
a folio is a large book

annotation.surface: A wine book that some people have put money into.
annotation.walkthrough: The definition is a descriptive phrase, not a synonym: the thing people have put their money in.
annotation.definitionFit: An investment portfolio is the collection of holdings into which an investor has put money.

entries.clue: Craftily singular English dramatist (5)

blocks.note: the grammar abbreviation
John Lyly, the Elizabethan playwright

annotation.surface: Praise for a playwright who is uniquely cunning.
annotation.walkthrough: John Lyly wrote Euphues and court comedies before Shakespeare's time; he is the crossword's go-to dramatist for these letters.
annotation.definitionFit: To do something slyly is to do it craftily, with quiet cunning.

entries.clue: One drawing on the support of the man in the street? (8,6)

annotation.definition: One drawing on the support of the man in the street?

blocks.note: the meant reading: someone who draws in chalk on the ground that holds up passers-by

blocks.clueFragment: of the man in the street
blocks.note: the surface reading: 'the man in the street' is the ordinary citizen, and 'drawing on his support' sounds like a politician courting votes

annotation.surface: A politician who relies on the backing of ordinary voters.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Drawing on the support of the man in the street' reads as courting public opinion; taken literally, the man in the street stands on the pavement, and someone is drawing on it.
annotation.definitionFit: A pavement artist makes chalk pictures on the paving stones, hoping passers-by will drop coins.

entries.clue: China pursuing evil game in court (9)

indicatorNotes.pursuing: to pursue is to follow, so this piece comes after the next one

blocks.note: bad = evil
Minton is a famous English porcelain maker

annotation.surface: A story of the Chinese chasing wickedness through the law courts.
annotation.walkthrough: The capital on 'China' makes it look like the country; it is fine porcelain, and Minton is a Staffordshire pottery name.
annotation.definitionFit: Badminton is a racket game played with a shuttlecock across a net on an indoor court.

entries.clue: Wind having estuary hotels suffering? (13)

indicatorNotes.suffering: letters that suffer are knocked about, damaged into a new order

blocks.note: anagram fodder, 13 letters
anagram indicator

annotation.surface: A gale battering the hotels along a river mouth.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface is a storm report, so 'Wind' sits naturally as the weather; this time it really is the weather.
annotation.definitionFit: A southeasterly is a wind blowing from the south-east.

entries.clue: Reported drive to pursue gold, being far from rich (7)

indicatorNotes.Reported: what is reported is passed on in speech, so we want the sound
indicatorNotes.to pursue: to pursue is to follow, so the sound comes after the gold

blocks.note: Au is the chemical symbol for gold
to steer is to drive; a stere is a cubic metre of timber, spelt differently but said the same

annotation.surface: Someone driven to chase gold because they are poor.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Rich' here means lavish or elaborate, so the definition fits plain, unadorned style as well as a hard life.
annotation.definitionFit: Something austere is severe and plain, without luxury, which is far from rich.

entries.clue: French poet intermittently pursued local man (9)

indicatorNotes.intermittently: on and off, so every other letter is taken

blocks.note: the 1st, 3rd, 5th and 7th letters of pursued
the word for man in the poet's own country, France

annotation.surface: A French poet was followed from time to time by a man from the area.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Local' refers back to the French poet: a man, locally speaking, is the French word. Sully Prudhomme won the first Nobel Prize in Literature in 1901.
annotation.definitionFit: Sully Prudhomme was a French poet and essayist, the first Nobel laureate in literature.

entries.clue: Last of stilton of doubtful quality is smelling bad (5)

indicatorNotes.Last of: only the final letter of the word is taken

blocks.note: the final letter of stilton
iffy = dubious, not quite right

annotation.surface: A cheese board remark: the last of the Stilton has gone off and stinks.
annotation.walkthrough: Stilton is a strong English blue cheese, so the surface is all too believable. Niff is British slang for a bad smell.
annotation.definitionFit: Niffy is informal British English for smelly.

entries.clue: Very best key army corps twice introducing lead shot (5,2,2,5)

indicatorNotes.twice: the key and corps are written out two times
indicatorNotes.introducing: the pair brings another piece in between them
indicatorNotes.shot: something shot is wrecked, so its letters are scrambled

blocks.note: C is a musical key
the Royal Electrical and Mechanical Engineers
LEAD rearranged, placed between the two copies
the second copy
the second copy

annotation.surface: An army unit gets its elite shooters in by firing lead.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Twice' doubles the whole key-plus-corps unit, and the jumbled lead is dropped into the gap between the two copies.
annotation.definitionFit: The French phrase, literally 'cream of the cream', means the very best of a group.

entries.clue: Way of working with cold royal in a derisive manner (9)

blocks.note: MO = modus operandi, Latin for method of operating
C = cold, as on a tap; 'with' adds it on
kingly = royal

annotation.surface: A royal, chilly and scornful at work.
annotation.walkthrough: Modus operandi is the detective-story phrase for a criminal's usual method.
annotation.definitionFit: To speak mockingly is to speak with derision, making fun of someone.

entries.clue: Request admission, needing to take food inside (8)

indicatorNotes.inside: the second piece goes within the first

blocks.note: entry = admission, the right to go in; split after the R
to take food is to eat

annotation.surface: Someone asks to be let in because they need a meal.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Request admission' reads as one phrase, knocking to be let in; the definition is only the first word, and admission is wordplay.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: an entreaty is an earnest plea, a request pressed hard.

entries.clue: Obscure record broken by rewritten novel (7)

indicatorNotes.broken by: the record is split open and the other letters are put in
indicatorNotes.rewritten: a novel rewritten comes out in a different order

blocks.note: an EP is an extended-play record, opened after the E
NOVEL rearranged

annotation.surface: An obscure record interrupted by a revised book.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Obscure' is a verb here, to hide from view, not the adjective the surface suggests.
annotation.definitionFit: To envelop something is to wrap it up so completely that it is hidden, which obscures it.

entries.clue: Sliding note at Prom? (10)

indicatorNotes.Sliding: letters that slide shift out of place, into a new order

blocks.note: anagram fodder, 10 letters
anagram indicator

annotation.surface: A singer at the Proms glides from one note to the next.
annotation.walkthrough: The Proms are the BBC's summer season of classical concerts in London. The whole clue is also the definition: a sliding note is just what a singer might produce there.
annotation.definitionFit: Portamento is a smooth glide in pitch from one note to another, in singing or on strings.

entries.clue: Some bones encountered on a historic site in Turkey (10)

blocks.note: met = encountered
'on' sets the next pieces after it
Tarsus, the ancient city where St Paul was born

annotation.surface: Bones unearthed on an archaeological dig in Turkey.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface is an archaeology find, which makes 'bones' look like remains; they are the ones in your foot. Tarsus is also the anatomical name for the ankle bones next door.
annotation.definitionFit: The metatarsus is the group of five long bones in the middle of the foot.

entries.clue: Cause metal to deform and weaken (10)

indicatorNotes.to deform: deformed letters are bent out of shape into a new order

blocks.note: anagram fodder, 10 letters
anagram indicator

annotation.surface: An engineer's instruction to bend metal until it gives.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface reads as one metalworking command; the definition is only the last word.
annotation.definitionFit: To emasculate is to deprive of strength or force, to weaken.

entries.clue: All rise stirred after priest is beginning on emotional anthem (2,12)

indicatorNotes.after: the mixed letters come after the priest
indicatorNotes.beginning on: only the first letter of the next word

blocks.note: a lama is a Tibetan Buddhist priest
ALL RISE rearranged
used as it stands
the first letter of emotional

annotation.surface: Everyone stands, moved, as a priest leads off a stirring national song.
annotation.walkthrough: 'All rise' is what the audience does for an anthem, and 'stirred' and 'emotional' feel like feelings; 'emotional' contributes only its first letter, and 'anthem' alone is the definition.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by example: this is one particular anthem, the French national one, written in 1792.

entries.clue: Where one is dying to add to share somehow (2,6,4)

indicatorNotes.somehow: put together in some way or other, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: anagram fodder, 12 letters
anagram indicator

annotation.surface: Someone longs to add to their shareholding one way or another.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Dying to' in the surface means eager; in the definition it is literal, so the definition ends at 'dying'.
annotation.definitionFit: Someone at death's door is very close to dying.

entries.clue: Indifferent about tango melody returning in a prolonged style (9)

indicatorNotes.about: the first piece goes around the rest
indicatorNotes.returning: the melody comes back, read from its end

blocks.note: so-so = indifferent, middling; opened after the second S
T is tango in the radio alphabet
a tune is a melody

annotation.surface: An uninspired dancer drags out a tango tune that keeps coming back.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Returning' reverses only the melody; the T goes in first, then the flipped tune, all inside the so-so.
annotation.definitionFit: Sostenuto is the musical direction for notes to be sustained, played in a prolonged way.

entries.clue: Quiet strike over new high-level railway in Chicago gets little money (8)

indicatorNotes.over: in a down answer, over means placed above, so these pieces come first

blocks.note: sh is the call for quiet
to rap is to strike sharply
the usual abbreviation
the El is Chicago's elevated railway

annotation.surface: A quiet industrial action over Chicago's new overhead railway leaves workers with little pay.
annotation.walkthrough: Shrapnel is British slang for loose change, a pocketful of small coins, from the fragments of an exploding shell.
annotation.definitionFit: Shrapnel is informal British English for small change: coins of low value.

entries.clue: A politician with current excuse (5)

blocks.note: used as it stands
short for a Liberal politician
I is the symbol for electric current; 'with' adds it

annotation.surface: A politician has an up-to-the-minute excuse ready.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Current' looks like 'up to date'; in physics formulas I stands for electric current.
annotation.definitionFit: An alibi is a claim of being elsewhere, and more loosely any excuse.

entries.clue: Spuds looking strange when brought back hot in dishes (8)

indicatorNotes.brought back: the word comes back, read from its end
indicatorNotes.in: the H goes inside the dishes

blocks.note: rum = odd, strange, in British slang
pies are dishes, opened after the P
H = hot, as on a tap

annotation.surface: Potatoes that look odd when they come back hot in their serving dishes.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Looking strange' seems to go together, but 'looking' is only the link: the spuds look like what the wordplay makes. Murphy is slang for a potato, from the Irish surname.
annotation.definitionFit: Murphies is informal British and Irish slang for potatoes, spuds.

entries.clue: Man’s place in his era is evolving (5,3)

indicatorNotes.evolving: something evolving changes its form, so the letters change order

blocks.note: anagram fodder, 8 letters
anagram indicator

annotation.surface: A thought on humankind's place in a changing age.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Man' is not mankind but the Isle of Man, which sits in the Irish Sea between Britain and Ireland.
annotation.definitionFit: The Isle of Man lies in the middle of the Irish Sea, so the sea is its place.

entries.clue: Hanging of worthless people, something which ends drama (6,7)

blocks.note: a shower is British slang for a useless lot of people
the curtain falls at the end of a play

annotation.surface: An execution of useless people brings the drama to an end.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Hanging' looks like an execution, which the grim surface supports; it is the noun, a thing that hangs. 'What a shower' is a British put-down for a useless bunch.
annotation.definitionFit: A shower curtain is a sheet hung around a shower, so it is literally a hanging.

entries.clue: Idly boasting vice-admiral — disgraceful (12)

blocks.note: the naval abbreviation
inglorious = shameful, disgraceful

annotation.surface: A verdict on a bragging senior naval officer who behaved shamefully.
annotation.walkthrough: The definition is the first two words, and it is the part of the surface that best describes the officer too.
annotation.definitionFit: Vainglorious means excessively proud and boastful, bragging with nothing to back it.

entries.clue: Machinery backing into car round aircraft (8)

indicatorNotes.backing: going backwards, so the word is read from its end
indicatorNotes.into: the reversed letters go inside the next pieces

blocks.note: auto = car
a rig is equipment or machinery, as on an oil rig
O is round in shape

annotation.surface: Machinery reverses into a car and ends up round an aircraft.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Car round' is a pair: the car and the O, with the backwards rig slotted between them.
annotation.definitionFit: An autogiro is an early rotor aircraft whose unpowered overhead blades spin in the airflow.

entries.clue: European friend’s after a lot of possibly Danish smoked beef (8)

indicatorNotes.after: the friend comes after the other piece
indicatorNotes.a lot of: most of the word, but not all: the last letter is dropped

blocks.note: a Danish is a pastry; drop its last letter
ami is French for friend

annotation.surface: A European friend is chasing a Danish pastry and some cured meat.
annotation.walkthrough: The ’s means 'is'. 'Possibly Danish' says a Danish is one example of a pastry, so the pastry is what gets cut.
annotation.definitionFit: Pastrami is highly seasoned smoked beef, often served sliced in sandwiches.

entries.clue: Wife of Odysseus out of confinement’s run away (5)

indicatorNotes.out of: the confinement is taken out of the wife's name

blocks.note: Penelope waited twenty years for Odysseus to return
a pen is an enclosure; its letters come off the front

annotation.surface: Odysseus's wife escapes captivity and runs off.
annotation.walkthrough: The ’s means 'is'. It is nicely apt: faithful Penelope, rid of her confinement, is the last person you would expect to run away with a lover.
annotation.definitionFit: To elope is to run away secretly, usually to marry.

entries.clue: Setter getting into panic over house cover protecting against fire (10)

indicatorNotes.getting into: the setter goes inside the panic
indicatorNotes.over: in a down answer, over means above, so this part comes first

blocks.note: a flap is a state of panic; opened after the A
the setter is me
the roof covers a house

annotation.surface: The setter panics about the cover on the house as fire breaks out.
annotation.walkthrough: In crosswords the setter refers to themselves as ME or I. 'In a flap' is British for flustered.
annotation.definitionFit: Something flameproof resists burning, so it protects against fire.

entries.clue: Lying Conservative interrupting second counting of votes (12)

indicatorNotes.interrupting: the Conservative breaks in between the other letters

blocks.note: s = second, the time abbreviation
a Tory is a member of Britain's Conservative Party
tellers count the votes in Parliament

annotation.surface: A dishonest Conservative breaks into a second recount of the votes.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface is election fraud. The Tory goes between S and TELLING; tellers are the officials who count votes, especially in a Commons division.
annotation.definitionFit: Storytelling is a gentle way of saying lying, telling tales.

entries.clue: Rash vote cast before end of day could be this? (9)

annotation.definition: Rash vote cast before end of day could be this?

indicatorNotes.cast: letters cast are thrown into a new order
indicatorNotes.end of: only the last letter of day

blocks.note: anagram fodder, 8 letters
anagram indicator
the last letter of day, added after the mix

annotation.surface: A snap vote held before the end of the day may be too hasty.
annotation.walkthrough: The whole clue does both jobs: a rash vote rushed through before close of day is exactly what the answer describes. 'Cast' fits votes and signals an anagram.
annotation.definitionFit: Overhasty means rash, done too quickly without due thought.

entries.clue: Against rum entitlement being pared down in fiddle? (10)

indicatorNotes.being pared down: shaved at both ends, so the outer letters of the phrase fall away

blocks.note: the phrase loses 'aga' at the front and 'itlement' at the back

annotation.surface: A protest against the sailors' rum ration being cut, with some fiddling going on.
annotation.walkthrough: The Royal Navy's daily rum ration was abolished in 1970, so a pared-down entitlement fits. The question mark marks fiddle as one example of the answer.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by example: the fiddle is one instrument among many, hence the question mark.

entries.clue: Elevated top international man that’s hard-working (8)

indicatorNotes.Elevated: raised up, so in a down answer the letters read bottom to top

blocks.note: a lid is a top
the usual abbreviation
a gent is a man

annotation.surface: A promoted top-flight international player known for his work rate.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Elevated top' reads as high-ranking; 'elevated' only flips the lid.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: diligent describes steady, careful effort, which is being hard-working.

entries.clue: Stone item for drawing unstarted pattern (7)

indicatorNotes.unstarted: never begun, so the first letter is missing

blocks.note: st = stone, the British unit of weight (14 lb)
a pencil without its first letter

annotation.surface: A stone drawing tool left unused and a design.
annotation.walkthrough: A stone is a British unit of body weight, abbreviated ST.
annotation.definitionFit: A stencil is a cut-out sheet used to reproduce a pattern, and by extension the pattern itself.

entries.clue: Convinced murderer must entertain regret regularly (7)

indicatorNotes.must entertain: to entertain a guest is to take them in, so the murderer holds the letters
indicatorNotes.regularly: at regular intervals, so every other letter

blocks.note: Cain killed his brother Abel in Genesis; opened after the C
the 2nd, 4th and 6th letters of regret

annotation.surface: A killer who is sure of himself must still show some remorse.
annotation.walkthrough: Cain, the first murderer in the Bible, is the standard crossword killer.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: someone certain of a thing holds it without doubt, so they are convinced.

entries.clue: Chain store with excellent way of presenting customer surveys? (8,6)

blocks.note: in British retail a multiple is a chain of shops
choice = excellent, top quality; 'with' joins it on

annotation.surface: A top-rated high-street chain has a new way of asking its customers questions.
annotation.walkthrough: A 'multiple' in British retail is a store with many branches. The question mark flags that surveys are only one use of the format.
annotation.definitionFit: Multiple-choice questions offer a list of answers to pick from, a common format for customer surveys.

entries.clue: Shut up about uncovered joint money (7)

indicatorNotes.about: the first word goes around the next
indicatorNotes.uncovered: with its outer layer removed, so the first and last letters go

blocks.note: to cage is to shut up; opened after the C
JOINT without its first and last letters

annotation.surface: A command to be quiet about some cash smuggled in with a joint of meat.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Shut up' sounds like 'be quiet'; it means to lock away, as in a cage.
annotation.definitionFit: Coinage is coins collectively, the metal money in circulation.

entries.clue: River among a number (6)

indicatorNotes.among: the R sits among the letters of the number

blocks.note: the usual map abbreviation, put inside the number
seven, opened after its second E

annotation.surface: A river counted as one among several.
annotation.walkthrough: 'River' does double duty: the whole clue is the definition, and its abbreviation R also goes inside the number. The Severn is Britain's longest river.
annotation.definitionFit: The Severn is the longest river in Britain, flowing from Wales into the Bristol Channel.

entries.clue: Detest house when a brother is round (5)

blocks.note: used as it stands
br = brother, opened after the B
ho = house, as in property listings

annotation.surface: Hating home life whenever a brother comes to visit.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Is round' sounds like a visit; it tells the brother to wrap around the house.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym, the stronger form: abhor is to loathe with a shudder, detest at its most intense.

entries.clue: Car needs time for inspection (5)

blocks.note: the German car make
t = time; 'needs' adds it

annotation.surface: A car has to be booked in for its annual check.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface is a garage service; the definition is the financial kind of check.
annotation.definitionFit: An audit is an official inspection, especially of accounts.

entries.clue: Current unit with long-term inmate — about one thing that might help him be heard? (9)

annotation.definition: thing that might help him be heard?

indicatorNotes.about: the inmate goes around the one

blocks.note: the amp is the unit of electric current
a lifer is serving a life sentence; opened after the F
I is the Roman one

annotation.surface: A prisoner serving life, with his electrics, gets a device so his case is heard.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Him' points back to the inmate: the definition is a device that would help the lifer be heard, which gives the clue its joke about a prisoner's appeal.
annotation.definitionFit: An amplifier boosts sound so that a speaker or instrument can be heard.

entries.clue: I am mature in vision (5)

blocks.note: I am shortened to I'M
to age is to mature

annotation.surface: Someone says they have grown up in the way they see things.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Mature' is a verb here, to grow older.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: a vision is a picture seen in the mind or before the eyes.

entries.clue: Contrary way in which Shakespeare wrote? (7)

blocks.note: the opposite, reversed
read as two words: his plays are mostly in lines of poetry

annotation.surface: A question about Shakespeare's awkward style.
annotation.walkthrough: The second sense splits the word in two: 'in verse' is how Shakespeare wrote, in blank verse. The question mark flags the play on words.
annotation.definitionFit: The first sense is a plain synonym for the opposite; the second splits into two words, since Shakespeare's plays are mostly in blank verse.

entries.clue: Silent protest of US soldier in base cut short (5)

indicatorNotes.in: the soldier is placed in the base, sitting inside its letters
indicatorNotes.cut short: the word loses its last letter

blocks.note: base = vile; drop the last letter, then open after the I
a GI is an American soldier

annotation.surface: An American soldier stages a quiet protest on a scaled-down army base.
